Glory to Limbus Company.

But more seriously: I have been with Project Moon since almost the start and am fully in support of their star rising. Not just because of their love for art and literature but that this is by far the least predatory Gacha in existence. Fantastic music (and hours of it), unique setting and writing that mostly doesnt treat you like you are iliterate.

There are some downsides:
1. The client can be a bit buggy / Mobile version is very hit or miss
2. Combat is not as well crafted as Library of Ruina and it can take a while till you get to combat that actually mandates you to think about team composition. But technically just about all content is doable with almost any team.
3. If you don't like turn based combat and fairly lengthy visual novel-esque dialogue this might not work for you - but it is free, so just try for yourself.

Going to be honest and keep it relatively short.

Is this a gacha? Yes. 

Is it predatory? NO, laughably easy to get anything you want, rates are good and every character is entirely farmable (no rng you get boxes you can pick shards from of one of the characters and then just get whatever you want, and the boxes are PLENTIFUL).

Is it the best gacha on market? No. I still think Arknights objectively takes that even if I'm not a tower defense person, but this is my personal favorite atm.

A little slow at the start but Canto 4 onwards is genuinely stellar writing, not just from a gacha standpoint but from storytelling in general. 

Combat is also excellent with genuine challenge and boss mechanics. BUT skill rng is genuine torture sometimes.


Overall: 8.5/10

I have barely played 8 hours and this game from the first canto is amazing.

Possibly my all time favorite gacha game for its ftp aspects, requiring a menial or major amount of thought per fight as the cantos progress. Personally haven't struggled much but I got possibly the best team at the time I began (Heishou) and used them until the HoS units cam out. The power creep is real but the units that are power creeping remind me much of LoR's power creep which was fairly drastic without much reason, leaving me with a familiar taste of difficulty in the recent canto. My main issue with this power creep is that LoR is a fully paid for game in which the gambling-like system is completely free and never timed by banners that boost drop rates, instead it's a gameplay mechanic incentivizing replaying stages for extra pages or necessary cards of a certain character that can make or break your progression. This game's powercreep, although not as bad thanks to the FTP mindset the game has, makes it a grind fest for players joining in a later canto needing units from a previous canto that are now locked basically making their progression waiting for that cantos units to come out in 2-3 week bursts between banners to progress properly without struggling through the story. Overall the story is a 10/10, gameplay is 7-8/10 and the gacha for being nearly free is 10/10.

526 hours into this game and I STILL don't understand everything.

And somehow that's part of why I love it.

Limbus Company is genuinely one of the best games I've played. The story, characters, art and writing are all super duper incredible, but the amount of depth this game has is insane.

I've played for over 500 hours and there are STILL mechanics where I'm sitting there like:

"what the hell does this do"

There's always something else to learn, some new team to build, some Identity or E.G.O to try, or some mechanic I somehow completely ignored for the last 200 hours.

And the best part?

You don't have to ducking pay to win.

You can spend money if you want to, but you never feel like the game is forcing you to open your wallet just to actually enjoy it. You can play, learn the systems, build your collection and progress without having to pay your way through everything.

And the OST?

HELLA BANGERS.

Project Moon does not miss. There are so many songs in this game that I genuinely listen to outside of the game.

The characters are also incredible. They're funny, insane, depressing, or somehow all three at once.

And I especially ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love Ricardo and the Middle.

Ricardo is one of those characters where the second he shows up, you KNOW you're about to have a bad time, and the whole Middle arc is just such a memorable part of the game for me.

526 hours later, I'm still learning things.

I'm still discovering mechanics.

I'm still listening to the OST outside the game.

I'm still getting attached to these idiots on the bus.

And somehow I'm still here. (I KNOW why.)

10/10.

Now excuse me, I have another mechanic I don't understand to completely ignore.

Durante just doesn't exist in normal content. Being a daily thing is so stupid. "Here's this cool ability that can change a fight, but wait! You can only use it once/twice per irl login". Should be per encounter. Entire system is straight stupid.

Later cantos you get quite a few abilites. Clear canto VIII? Cool. Now your very first durannte can be used twice per irl day. wtf. Entire system is genuinely non existent for 99% of the game anyways. In story you get uses for free because you can get softlocked. In railway, you get free uses per run. But in every other content (especially mirror dungeons), you're locked to the garbage "per irl day" use case.

However, durante isn't even needed half the time. Got the new ids from this season? Cool, now you can solo the entire extreme difficulty mirror dungeon with 1 unit. Nursefather yi sang solos. Full buffed blade of the house of spiders ryoshu solos. 

Durante systems needs a change. Way too unusable. Basically jsut sits there until you need it, and even then, I'll likely never ever use it, because I'll prob never use it. MAYBE if my yi sang 9 coin attack or fully buffed ryoshu can't handle it, but so far, they breeze through practically everything. Power creep kinda ruined durante. Maybe if this was early LC, but current LC durante just sucks.

Other than that, the game is fun. Didn't play the past project moon games, but this is one of the 'better gacha games' i played. Needs some addressing to power creep and such. Glad they aren't as afraid to change things like epic seven, and some of the other games.

Incredible Story, Compelling Gameplay, and genuinely one of the most generous Gacha's I have ever played. 

Story:
It is a rich story with interesting characters overcoming their traumas and pasts. It starts slowly, and has some pacing problems at first, but after they hit their stride it has been nothing but peak after peak with each major story release.

Gameplay:
Tactical, Strategic, Simple
The Gameplay is a turn-based brawler. I wont go into the details because its complex, but it has a good amount of depth, and team building is very fun. And many of the bosses are extremely thematic in their mechanics, and often, we get IDs of those bosses that we can use ourselves. Which is very cool. Its Simpler than their previous game Library of Ruina, but more than suitable for what theyre going for.

Gacha:
This is one of the most generous gachas I've played. Grinding out IDs isnt nothing, but its far easier than 90% of the Gachas ive played. You get just under 6 rolls a week from doing weekly grinding. And the battle pass is easy to max out by doing the same weekly objectives. Plus the battlepass gives you more pity currency, and is the main way you will get IDs

Identities (IDs) are mirror world versions of the characters. So instead of having 500 characters, they have 12, and they release different mirror world versions of those characters that are usually relevant to the story at hand. This prevents the typical character bloat of other Gachas and allows each character to explored with a lot of depth and care, and they do it marvelously.

Genuinely recommend it if you like Gachas, or if any of this appealed to you. Its a worthwhile journey.
